scope: beat-upstream 14-day screen, first run with the repaired feed path

version_gate.note: Two gate bugs were fixed after the run and the survivor list re-scored. Records often put the whole affected range in the version field as '< 2.0.5' rather than filling lessThan, which the parser read as an introduced version; and the tag-lag gate only inspected tags newer than the packaged version, so a tree already carrying the fix looked like an opportunity. PrivateBin CVE-2026-55891 reached the shortlist through both: nixpkgs packages 2.0.6 and the fix shipped in 2.0.5.

note: Compare with beat-upstream-summary-2026-09-01.json: 0 survivors of 6297, which was feed data loss rather than absence of opportunity. The version gate landed after this run, so the 76 out-of-range rejects were computed by re-scoring the survivor list; a future run applies the gate inline. Survivors are candidates, not verified patches: each still has to pass Patcher, Reviewer, a discriminating reproducer and cert.

precision_gates.note: Three gates added after the run and applied by re-scoring; a future run applies them inline. Together they remove 106 of 181 raw survivors as false positives, each of which would otherwise have cost a bootstrap. The classes are: a pname collision whose versions do not overlap the affected range (haskellPackages.zephyr matching Zephyr RTOS); an affected range written inline in the version field as '< 2.0.5' rather than in lessThan (PrivateBin); and an advisory citing an older commit the packaged release already contains (filebrowser cites a 2020 commit while packaging 2.63.23). A fourth pass added GitLab to the tag and containment queries and matched tags by name suffix as well as parsed version, since OpenRGB tags releases 'release_candidate_1.0rc3.1'. That dropped the three OpenRGB candidates, whose pinned source already carries the fix. A fifth gate compares a package-set attr's language with the fix repository's primary language: haskellPackages.redis against redis/redis (C) is a name collision, not the same software. Eight fell to it.
